title: What's Love Got to Do with It?
coreMove: Use labels as tools, not verdicts: ask what history makes the symptoms cohere, then aim care at the repeated injury instead of chasing each alarm.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A patient can leave with more labels while the developmental history remains hidden.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a clinician using history to test whether labels point to one old pattern.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Health risks may look like scattered behavior problems unless the adversity cluster is named.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn a list of adult risks into a search for clustered early adversity.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Billing pressure can reward symptom codes while discouraging root-cause questions.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how a rejected claim can reveal what the record failed to connect.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A relapse review can blame poor choices or examine the old adversity behind coping.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use ACE findings to read relapse as part of a broader survival pattern.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Students can be sorted by behavior before anyone asks about caregiving injury.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Make the intake form ask about history without turning it into accusation.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A benefits plan may fund separate adult risks while missing the adversity pattern underneath.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a benefits map changing after ACE clustering is considered.
